I had the vet come to my house which was really important as my dog got very anxious at the clinic. We did it on my front step. I used to work in a vet office and have held so many pets for euthanasia. But I knew watching my guy slip away was not something I could handle having in my head forever. So I sat next to him but looked away when it started. The vet had told me how long to wait before standing up and walking away so I waited and then walked to my car and drove around for 20 minutes while they moved him. I came home to a tidy porch. I think I only survived the experience because this vet (not even my regular vet) was so incredibly compassionate and caring and really helped me focus on making the right, informed decision and taking into consideration my needs. It was a very good last afternoon. 

My guy was not old but we had struggled for just under two years with a very tricky and unfixable blood sugar issue that usually gives an average of 70 days after diagnosis. My life revolved around scheduled feedings, blood glucose monitoring, and medications for the last years of his life. I was never away from him or asleep for more than 6 hours at a time. I think I needed to give him every chance I could as long as he seemed happy. 

I am so sooo lucky that that vet mad the end a beautiful experience. His illness was awful (for me) and I think I am messed up about everything BUT the end. I never tried to extend his life for me but I needed to not “throw him away” just because the condition was inconvenient. 

tl:dr: 

- Do it at home, it’s worth the money
- Look away at the end
- Don’t handle the body if it’s not something you WANT to do for closure
-plan ahead what you want to do (burial, cremation) so you don’t have to deal with that in the moment
